chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Two twigs are placed for the deceased, one on the right and the other on the left.

key_terms.جَرِيدَتَانِ: Two twigs or small branches, used here in a ritual context for the deceased.

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual significance of placing twigs for the deceased in Shia burial practices?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi highlights the Sunnah of placing two palm fronds (jariadat) on the right and left sides of the deceased, a practice rooted in the traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt. It reflects the meticulous attention to detail in Shia burial rites, symbolizing comfort and preparation for the soul's journey in the grave (Barzakh).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Two twigs would be placed for the deceased – one of the right and the other one on the left’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muhammad ibn Sanaa ‘ah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
two pieces of al-Jaridah (twig of palm tree) are placed with a deceased: one on the right and the other on the left side.’”
